artifact: Runtime Verification, 'End-to-End Formal Verification of Ethereum 2.0 Deposit Smart Contract (Solidity Reimplementation)', https://github.com/runtimeverification/deposit-contract-verification (report deposit-contract-verification.pdf; bytecode spec bytecode-verification/deposit-spec.ini)
property: The compiled bytecode of the deposit contract refines the incremental Merkle tree algorithm, which is proved equivalent to the full-tree construction; deposit/get_deposit_root behave per the bytecode spec.
model: Source commit 2ac62c4 compiled by solc v0.6.8 with --optimize-runs 5000000; KEVM semantics; a single transaction, assuming well-formed calldata.
trusted_base: non-mechanized parts of the algorithm-correctness proof
assumptions: calldata is well-formed with no garbage bytes
single-transaction scope: no transaction-level or off-chain behavior
the deployed bytecode is the verified bytecode
deployed: Mainnet DepositContract at 0x00000000219ab540356cBB839Cbe05303d7705Fa, Sourcify exact match: solc 0.6.11+commit.5ef660b1, optimizer runs 5000000, evmVersion istanbul. Measured 2026-10-08: deployed runtime code (via eth_getCode) equals RV's verified runtime bytecode byte-for-byte except the trailing 53-byte CBOR metadata (IPFS hash and solc version 0.6.8 vs 0.6.11).
gap: The report's guarantee is conditioned on solc v0.6.8 output, but mainnet runs a solc 0.6.11 build; the gap closes only by comparing bytes, which shows identical executable code with differing metadata. The proof also covers one transaction with well-formed calldata and excludes off-chain processing of deposits by the beacon chain.
